create.name: Gay Buddhist Fellowship
create.bio:
The Gay Buddhist Fellowship (GBF) is a San Francisco sangha that belongs to no single school of Buddhism. Each week it invites a teacher, from Zen, Theravada, Tibetan or other lineages, to speak on how the Dharma meets queer life today, and it welcomes people of every race, background, gender and sexuality. It is run by volunteers under a board of directors and is supported by donations.

The community meets on Sunday mornings, in person at the SF Buddhist Center and on Zoom, for meditation and a talk, and holds an online sangha on Wednesday evenings. It also organises day-long and residential retreats, among them a spring retreat at Vajrapani, and sends a quarterly newsletter, including to people in prison. Its Sunday talks form a long-running podcast, the Gay Buddhist Forum, whose archive of more than nine hundred recordings reaches back to the mid-1990s; since 2024 the talks have also been posted to YouTube, where the back catalogue has been uploaded too.

flags: gaybuddhistfellowship@gmail.com is the organisation's general inbox (brand inbox).

Tagline reads 'Wisdom for Liberation and Social Action', and the About page discusses bias and privilege; the talks themselves are Dharma teaching, so not treated as political-centred. Owner may wish to review.

Teachers file has no links: Walt Opie (walt-opie on dev) appears on the site's podcast page as a guest Sunday speaker only, not as a teacher of the sangha; the same standard was used for other channel-hosts in this batch. Owner may choose to link him with evidence https://gaybuddhist.org/podcast/.
Only one photo: the channel's 'Gay Buddhist Forum' logo avatar. The site's own logo is 200 px wide and its banner is a generic Buddha image, so neither was used.
Several uploads appear twice on the channel (dated and undated copies); only one copy of each used.
Possible future listings: Sean Feit Oakes, Roshi David Blackwell, Dorothy Hunt, Donald Rothberg, Liên Shutt (not on Spiritpedia).
